title: A thermal ultimatum, a UWB omission and a second price ladder
summary: This week's S27 reporting centred on silicon. Seoul Economic Daily reported that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheated and throttled in Galaxy S27 Ultra testing, that Samsung set a mid-October deadline, and that the Exynos 2700 is the fallback; Qualcomm called the account inaccurate. Alongside it, MIIT listings read through one tipster put UWB on the Pro and Ultra but not the base or Plus, GalaxyClub narrowed the 16MP selfie upgrade to the two premium models, and a 13 October ladder contradicted the 8 October prices. Ice Universe's bezel and camera-bump measurements arrived with conflicting comparisons, and two display claims — DC dimming and a Privacy Display v2 — stayed single-source.

claims.title: An Exynos Ultra may be back on the table
claims.summary: Money Today reports development of an Exynos 2700 Galaxy S27 Ultra for some markets, alongside the Snapdragon model. Android Authority highlights the change against earlier Snapdragon-only expectations. A 24 September aggregation repeats the Exynos Ultra reading and names South Korea and parts of Europe as the expected Exynos markets with the United States staying on Snapdragon, but it names no source or filing and is carried here as context rather than support. In October the picture firmed up: Samsung's latest in-house chip went into mass production with the base, Plus and Pro as its intended homes, and separate reporting says an Exynos-powered Ultra prototype is in testing even though MX has not ruled on the model. On 9 October that reading changed again: reporting attributed to the Naver blogger Lanzuk says Samsung has no plans for an Exynos Ultra in any market, with the Exynos 2700 going to the base, Plus and Pro in most of Europe, Asia and Africa and Snapdragon reserved for North America and China. On 16 October Seoul Economic Daily reported that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 failed Samsung's thermal checks in Ultra testing and that the Exynos 2700 is the fallback if it is not fixed, which puts the Exynos Ultra back in play; a 17 October relay says the Ultra decision is still open.
claims.assessment: Specific industry reporting, and the October production and prototype stories point the same way, but development, testing and an order book are not a retail launch. Regions, chip branding and sustained performance remain unconfirmed, and the archive keeps the Snapdragon-only reading alive because Samsung itself has not settled the Ultra. The Ultra reading has now swung twice in eight days on supply-chain attributions this archive has never read at source, so neither the Exynos Ultra nor the worldwide Snapdragon reading is treated as settled. The 16 October thermal report supplies a concrete mechanism for an Exynos Ultra without establishing that one has been ordered.

claims.title: A wider camera island, not isolated rings
claims.summary: SamMobile describes OnLeaks-based CAD renders with a horizontal rectangular rear camera bar. Android Authority separately describes Sonny Dickson images with a wide camera plateau. On 17 October Ice Universe shared a video of another S27 Ultra case showing the same horizontal bar, relayed by Sammy Fans.
claims.assessment: Two attributed image-report chains point in a similar direction, but neither establishes the final production design. We could not inspect the original Android Headlines article.

claims.title: Three rear cameras in the newer render report
claims.summary: SamMobile describes three rear cameras in the reported CAD-based design. That conflicts with Android Central’s earlier description of a main camera plus three 50-megapixel lenses.
claims.assessment: Counting lenses in an alleged design is not a confirmed camera specification. Both accounts are retained; the newer article alone does not settle it, and the September telephoto reporting disputes the module behind the third lens while leaving the count itself open.

claims.title: Built-in magnetic charging is suggested
claims.summary: Android Authority interprets a circular rear cutout in the apparent renders as possible integrated Qi2 magnets. SamMobile says 25-watt Qi2 charging is likely.
claims.assessment: This is an interpretation of images and secondary reporting, not certification or a verified charging test. No charging speed is treated as established.

claims.title: The earlier account still described four lenses
claims.summary: Android Central’s report of Anthony’s tip lists a 200-megapixel main camera and three 50-megapixel lenses: ultrawide, 5× telephoto and another telephoto.
claims.assessment: Retained as a conflicting report, not silently deleted or declared false. The later three-camera account has not been officially resolved.

claims.title: Snapdragon-only for the Ultra is argued in both directions
claims.summary: Android Central’s earlier specification report names Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro for Galaxy without an Exynos variant. Android Authority explicitly says the newer Exynos report contradicts prior Snapdragon-only claims. On 9 October a report attributed to Lanzuk on Naver revived the worldwide Snapdragon reading for the Ultra specifically, saying Samsung has no plans to ship an Exynos Ultra in any market while the rest of the family takes the Exynos 2700 outside North America and China.
claims.assessment: The earlier specification list is not proof of worldwide exclusivity. Snapdragon and Exynos may coexist; naming and regional availability remain unsettled. The claim now has support from both the original specification reporting and the newest allocation report, but both come from unattributed supply-chain talk rather than a Samsung statement, order document or filing.

claims.title: A 6.9-inch Privacy Display is tipped
claims.summary: Android Central reports Anthony’s claim of a 6.9-inch QHD+ Privacy Display for the Ultra.
claims.assessment: One tipster chain, no panel document or production unit examined. The September ETNews reading now narrows Privacy Display to the Pro and Ultra, so the all-models account is preserved here as the contradicted side of a live disagreement rather than as a settled display specification.

claims.title: 5,534 mAh rated; advertised capacity still an estimate
claims.summary: GalaxyClub says information it viewed gives the Ultra a 5,534 mAh rated battery. It estimates an advertised capacity around 5,700 mAh, possibly 5,800 mAh; Android Authority relays the 5,700 mAh estimate.
claims.assessment: Rated and typical capacity are different measures. The original article's second "rated" label is internally inconsistent; we preserve its estimates while noting that the 5,534 mAh rated figure now also appears in the September 3C coverage, which is firmer provenance than the July relay.

claims.title: Silicon-carbon chemistry is plausible, not demonstrated
claims.summary: GalaxyClub infers silicon-carbon chemistry indirectly from the reported capacity increase. 9to5Google also relays a silicon-carbon rumor, noting that lineup coverage and capacities were unclear.
claims.assessment: A capacity estimate does not prove cell chemistry. This is a separate, lower-confidence claim from the rated-capacity report.

claims.title: A 16-megapixel front camera is reported
claims.summary: 9to5Google’s roundup lists a 16-megapixel autofocus selfie camera for the Ultra. GalaxyClub also describes a new 16-megapixel front camera.
claims.assessment: These reports share GalaxyClub provenance. Sensor shape and stabilization are not established by this record.

claims.title: A new Pro turns the family's trio into a quartet
claims.summary: CAD render reports describe four Galaxy S27 models instead of three: the base S27, an S27+, a new S27 Pro and the S27 Ultra. GSMArena describes the Pro as a smaller Ultra without an S Pen, and Android Headlines reads the Plus CAD as proof the Plus survives. SamMobile's case images show the same quartet. October brought the project's first hardware trace: components and OLED panels reported in production, and screen-protector listings for all four models.
claims.assessment: Several outlets agree on a four-model reading, but they are reading render art rather than a Samsung document, and the segmentation is inferred from images. A rumored S27 Edge would make five. Nothing here is an announcement.

claims.title: The base S27 barely leaves the S26 behind
claims.summary: CAD renders of the base S27 show an oval three-ring camera bump in the top-left corner, flat panels and a flat frame, with reported dimensions of 149.75 × 71.88 × 7.25 mm and a 6.3-inch display. 9to5Google notes the base model looks nothing like the redesigned Ultra.
claims.assessment: Three outlets describe the same Android Headlines render set, so this is shared provenance rather than three independent leaks. The dimensions are render-derived and the chipset is still described as open.

claims.title: The Pro inherits the Ultra's body but not its periscope
claims.summary: GSMArena reports the S27 Pro at 154.06 × 73.77 × 7.95 mm with a roughly 6.6-inch display, sharing the Ultra's 200-megapixel main and 50-megapixel ultrawide but using a 12-megapixel 3x telephoto instead of a periscope, plus a rumored 5,200 mAh battery. SamMobile's case-render report says 5x optical zoom may stay exclusive to the Ultra.
claims.assessment: Two outlets point the same way and neither examined hardware. The discriminating claim is the telephoto, which is why this is filed under cameras; the size and battery figures remain renderer claims and the Ultra's own zoom arrangement is unresolved.

claims.title: A camera plateau may replace the horizontal bar
claims.summary: Notebookcheck reports that an Ice Universe design sketch, which the leaker later said was the S27 Ultra, shows a raised camera plateau closer to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro treatment, and that the earlier Pixel-like horizontal bar is out. SamMobile's 2 September case images show the Pro and Ultra with the same raised plateau.
claims.assessment: This directly conflicts with the OnLeaks CAD camera bar already in this archive. Two of the best-known render sources currently point at different rear designs, so the conflict is preserved rather than resolved. None of it is official evidence.

claims.title: An S27 Edge is rumored, and the two accounts disagree
claims.summary: Two X accounts posted on 2 September that a Galaxy S27 Edge is in development for 2027. @kro_roe described a 5.8-inch display in a low-4 mm chassis with a 4,300 mAh battery; @SPYGO19726 replied hours later claiming a 6.8-inch body at 5.4 mm. SamMobile, Notebookcheck and tech-ish all report both readings. A 23 September round-up goes the other way, describing the new Pro as replacing the Edge line entirely rather than joining it.
claims.assessment: Neither account gave a source, and the two readings differ on the most basic property of the device. The archive keeps both opposed instead of choosing one. Notebookcheck calls this the only very early rumor in the family. An Edge would likely arrive later in 2027 than the main quartet.

claims.title: Charging stays at 25 W and 45 W
claims.summary: Android Authority reports that China's 3C registry lists 25 W wired charging for the base S27 and 45 W for the S27 Plus, relayed from tipster Abhishek Yadav on X. The report notes the base model would still trail the Galaxy S26 FE, and that the S27 Ultra and Pro may keep or improve on last year's 60 W.
claims.assessment: A regulatory listing is firmer evidence than a render, but this archive did not inspect the registry entry and the relay is a single chain. The same registry later put the Pro and Ultra at 60 W, which the base model's 25 W does not share.

claims.title: Magnetic arrays are read into all four CAD sets
claims.summary: Notebookcheck's reading of the Ice Universe CAD renders says all four S27 models include built-in magnetic arrays for magnetic chargers and accessories. Android Authority separately reports built-in magnets for MagSafe-style latching across the series, though it says wireless charging speed may not change.
claims.assessment: This extends the earlier Qi2 interpretation from a circular cutout on the Ultra to the whole family. CAD geometry is not certification, and the archive still holds no charging test or certification document.

claims.title: The speaker grille moves to the right on three models
claims.summary: Notebookcheck reports that in the leaked CAD renders the base S27, the S27+ and the rumored S27 Pro move the bottom-firing speaker grille to the right of the USB-C port, while the Ultra keeps the left-side placement used on the S26 generation.
claims.assessment: One outlet's reading of CAD geometry, with an ergonomic rationale attached to it. Useful as a design detail, but it is not a measured audio specification and the archive has not seen a teardown or part listing.

claims.title: A leaked die shot fixes the Exynos 2700's outline
claims.summary: SamMobile reports that a SemiAnalysis die shot and annotated floorplan show the Exynos 2700 with a 10-core CPU (two C2 Ultra cores at 4.24 GHz and 3.36 GHz, eight C2 Pro cores), an Xclipse 970 GPU with 16 compute units, a 24 MB system-level cache, four LPDDR6 PHYs and no integrated modem, built on Samsung Foundry's SF2P 2 nm process.
claims.assessment: An inspectable floorplan is firmer evidence than a text tip, but it is still a leak, and claims that the chip beats Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 are not measured. The archive attaches this to the chipset question rather than to a shipping part.

claims.title: The base S27 is tipped for a 4,900 mAh cell and a Sony sensor
claims.summary: GSMArena relays that the base S27 may use a new Sony main camera sensor and a silicon-carbon battery at 4,900 mAh, up from the S26's 4,300 mAh, while leaving the chipset open between Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Exynos 2700. tech-ish separately relays a July report saying Samsung was undecided about silicon-carbon on the base model because of cost.
claims.assessment: One relayed claim set attached to a render report. A September reading of the 3C filings puts the base model at 4,300 mAh instead, so the 4,900 mAh figure is retained only as the contradicted side of the disagreement, and the chemistry decision is described elsewhere as unresolved on cost.

claims.title: M16 OLED for the Pro and Ultra, M14 for the base and Plus
claims.summary: ETNews reports that Samsung Display will supply M16 OLED panels for the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, with Color Filter-on-Encapsulation and Privacy Display, while the base S27 and S27 Plus move up from M13 to M14. Notebookcheck and SamMobile repeat the split the same day. The 8 October price leak relays the same divide through @phonefuturist, describing the lower tier as M14+ rather than plain M14 and tying Privacy Display to the M16 panel on the Pro and Ultra alone.
claims.assessment: One Korean industry-sourcing chain relayed by several outlets within hours, so the repetition is not independent corroboration. The tier split is specific and internally consistent, and M16 already ships in rival handsets, but no panel specification is officially confirmed. The M14+ wording refines rather than reverses the split: the base and Plus stay a tier below their siblings, and what moves is the panel generation rather than which models get the privacy feature.

claims.title: Privacy Display narrows to the Pro and Ultra
claims.summary: Reporting traced to ETNews and read through GSMArena, SamMobile and Notebookcheck says only the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra get Privacy Display, leaving the base and Plus out. That reverses a July report that every model except a future FE would carry it, and a mid-September round-up still repeats the all-models version. A 25 September round-up repeats the same two-model reading. The 8 October price leak ties Privacy Display to the M16 panel tier again, giving it to the Pro and Ultra and leaving the base and Plus without it.
claims.assessment: The newer claim is the more specific one - Flex Magic Pixel panels plus COE on two models - but it comes from the same sourcing chain that has now changed twice. The archive keeps both readings open and does not treat the July account as dead.

claims.title: The four models' screen sizes take shape
claims.summary: ETNews lists a 6.27-inch Galaxy S27, a 6.66-inch S27 Plus, a 6.47-inch S27 Pro and a 6.89-inch S27 Ultra, with Samsung Display expected to supply every panel. SamMobile repeats the same four figures and Notebookcheck reports the same range.
claims.assessment: Panel-supply reporting usually carries firmer dimensions than render-based guesses, and a Pro that lands smaller than the Plus matches the design story, but these are unannounced sizes from a single sourcing chain.

claims.title: 3C listings give the Pro and Ultra 60 W and larger rated cells
claims.summary: China's 3C registry entries linked to SM-S957 and SM-S958 show 60 W wired charging at 20 V/3 A for both the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, and separate battery filings are reported at 5,087 mAh rated for the Pro and 5,534 mAh rated for the Ultra - figures outlets convert to roughly 5,200 mAh and 5,700 mAh advertised.
claims.assessment: A regulatory filing is stronger evidence than a tip, but this archive did not inspect the registry entry and the model-number mapping is an outlet inference. Rated and expected advertised capacities stay separate, and the 60 W ceiling only matches what the S26 Ultra already offers.

claims.title: A single 4x telephoto was under evaluation for the Ultra
claims.summary: A late-August tip attributed to @phonefuturist described Samsung weighing one 50-megapixel 1/1.9-inch telephoto at 4x optical zoom in place of the Ultra's separate 3x and 5x cameras, with five Ultra prototypes in test and a hardware decision said to be due around 9 September.
claims.assessment: An account-level tip read only through relays, with no document behind it. The surrounding write-ups made clear the configuration was being compared against the existing 5x module on cost, not chosen, and by late September Gagadget describes the larger 4x option as dead after Ice Universe restated the 5x-only setup, so this report is retained as the abandoned side of the argument.

claims.title: The 5x telephoto looks set to carry over after all
claims.summary: Ice Universe called the 4x 1/1.9-inch report false and said the Ultra keeps its 5x 1/2.52-inch module; two days later two outlets attributed the same 50-megapixel Sony 5x arrangement to Roland Quandt. GSMArena also records the Pro as a 200-megapixel main, 50-megapixel ultrawide and 12-megapixel 3x telephoto. Ice Universe then restated the 5x-only setup explicitly on 29 September, describing the module as carried over unchanged at a 1/2.52-inch sensor and f/2.9, which the outlets read as closing the 4x question.
claims.assessment: Two named accounts with long track records point the same way, and the three-camera geometry is separately visible in the OnLeaks CAD render — yet neither original post was read, and a carried-over module changes nothing a buyer can check before launch. The 3x-removal thread now has its own report.

claims.title: Warmer colour and reworked Log video are tipped for the Ultra
claims.summary: An X account, @WalleGalaxy, says the S27 Ultra keeps 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps while gaining updated Samsung Log and APV support for wider dynamic range, plus an overhauled photo pipeline tuned for warmer, more natural colour than the S26 Ultra. A 16-megapixel autofocus selfie camera is repeated alongside.
claims.assessment: The camera count and front-camera details overlap with earlier chains, but the colour and codec claims rest on one account that Android Authority itself flags as not established. Software tuning cannot be checked before launch, and no Samsung statement covers it.

claims.title: A 7,000 mAh, S Pen-less prototype was reportedly rejected
claims.summary: Android Police, relaying X user Kro and Android Authority, reports that Samsung tested Galaxy S27 Ultra units without an S Pen slot and with a 7,000 mAh cell, then settled on a 5,700-6,000 mAh target with silicon-carbon anode chemistry of the kind used in the Fold 8 generation.
claims.assessment: The rejected prototype would explain why earlier capacity chatter ranged so widely, but the account published no document and the surviving figure is a target rather than a specification. Chemistry is inferred from another product line, not from a filing.

claims.title: The base S27's display may be engineered down to a price
claims.summary: PhoneArena's running round-up says Samsung is weighing BOE panels for the base model, may leave it on the older M13 material and is evaluating third-party display driver ICs from Anapass, DB Global Chip, Wonik D2I and Novatek - measures that would sit against the M14 upgrade reported for the base and Plus.
claims.assessment: Each item is individually uncorroborated and presented as an option rather than a decision. If any of it lands, the base model's screen would be the first part of the family to move backwards, so the archive holds it against the ETNews M14 claim without settling the question.

claims.title: LPDDR5X for the base and Plus, LPDDR6 held for the Ultra
claims.summary: PhoneArena, citing the Korean outlet The Bell, reports Samsung qualifying Micron LPDDR5X for the Galaxy S27 series and reserving LPDDR6 for the Ultra tier on cost grounds, with Micron's opening pricing described as well above Samsung's own memory division. Reports from 22 to 25 September keep the split but add a tier caveat: GSMArena relays a Korean rumor that LPDDR6 and UFS 5.1 are targeted at the Pro and Ultra yet may reach only the higher storage tiers, and that the base and Plus will not move to the new standards at all, while Gagadget relays a Micron LPDDR6 price premium as the reason the plan could fall back.
claims.assessment: A memory-standard split between four flagships would matter over the life of the devices, but it rests on one relayed Korean report and a supplier earnings remark rather than a Samsung statement or a filing this archive read. The tier caveat matters more than the headline: it would leave the same phone shipping two memory standards depending on which SKU a buyer picks.

claims.title: The chip tiers look set to widen between the Ultra and the rest
claims.summary: PhoneArena's round-up says Qualcomm is splitting Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 into standard and Pro versions, with the Pro part going to the S27 Ultra and the standard part to the base and Plus, while Samsung's own Exynos 2700 evaluation is described as beating both in CPU, GPU, AI and efficiency tests. On 9 October the regional half of the split was restated through Lanzuk: Exynos 2700 for the base, Plus and Pro across most of Europe, Asia and Africa, Snapdragon mainly for North America and China, and Snapdragon alone in the Ultra.
claims.assessment: Aggregated from tipsters and Korean supply-chain reporting rather than read at source here. Pre-release benchmark claims about unreleased silicon are the least stable class of leak, and the regional split that decides what buyers actually get is still unconfirmed. The tiering itself is consistent across reports; what keeps moving is which models the Exynos tier covers, which is exactly the part this archive cannot verify.

claims.title: The base and Plus cells may be smaller than the archive first heard
claims.summary: A 20 September aggregation of the 3C coverage repeats a readings-based figure of 4,300 mAh for the base model and 4,900 mAh for the Plus, alongside the already-reported 25 W and 45 W charging ceilings. The 4,300 mAh base figure sits against the archive's August reading of 4,900 mAh for the base model.
claims.assessment: Two relayed readings of different filings disagree about the base model, and neither this archive nor the write-up it read inspected the Chinese registry entry. The Plus figure matching the earlier base figure is exactly the kind of coincidence that argues for caution rather than confirmation.

claims.title: Four models on one stage in the first quarter of 2027, an FE later
claims.summary: Reporters converge on a January or February 2027 Unpacked for the Galaxy S27 family, with ETNews saying simply the first quarter and SamMobile describing a five-model year in which an S27 FE follows around mid-2027. Firmware testing for One UI 9.5 is reported to be behind the S26 cycle's pace. A 25 September round-up frames the window as February or March and counts five phones with the Edge included. The Exynos 2700 production report adds a physical clock: a three-to-four-month wafer-to-product interval, which its reporter reads as fitting a February or March launch.
claims.assessment: Launch timing is the easiest claim to get roughly right and the hardest to pin down exactly. No invitation exists, Samsung has said nothing about the S27 series, and the FE reference is a lineup expectation rather than a commitment.

claims.title: A Pro at Ultra money, an Ultra at $1,399 and higher prices outside the US and Korea
claims.summary: A late-August rumor put the expected US ladder at $899 for the Galaxy S27, $1,099 for the Plus, $1,299 for the Pro and $1,499 for the Ultra, with the new Pro taking the Ultra's old slot. A mid-September round-up, by contrast, says nothing has leaked on base and Plus pricing and that the S26's post-increase levels may simply hold. A late-September to early-October Korean rumor then put every model up, not just the Ultra, with the base increase in the high KRW 130,000 range and steeper steps between storage tiers. On 8 and 9 October the ladder was restated through a @phonefuturist post at $899, $1,099, $1,299 and $1,399 for the United States, with global prices a tier higher at $999, $1,199, $1,399 and $1,499 to $1,549, and the post pushed back on the expectation of an across-the-board increase because Samsung had already raised prices on the existing S26 line. 9to5Google, Sammy Fans, Trusted Reviews and PhoneArena relayed the figures; neither the post nor the Android Headlines page carrying it was read here.
claims.assessment: Both readings are expectations, not listings or filings, and they disagree about how much has actually been learned. Component cost pressure is cited on both sides, so the archive records the ladder as a rumor and marks the base and Plus figures as unverified. The October list contradicts the 30 September Korean reading that every model and storage tier rises: it holds the US base at $899 and puts the Ultra below the late-August expectation, while the non-US columns sit above the S26 levels the same post compares against. Both readings are kept, and the leak's own caveat that memory supply could still move the figures applies to either.

claims.title: Twelve gigabytes everywhere and one 16 GB tier
claims.summary: Four accounts across four days describe the same ladder: 12 GB with 256 GB or 512 GB on the Galaxy S27 and S27+, 12 GB with 256 GB, 512 GB or 1 TB on the new Pro, and 12 GB with 256 GB or 512 GB plus a lone 16 GB with 1 TB option on the Ultra. SammyGuru attributes the list to the tipster @wallegalaxy and adds a possible 128 GB tier outside most markets; Android Authority attributes it to the leaker Lanzuk on the Korean blog Naver, who cites Weibo posts and Korean industry sources; GSMArena reports the same table from an unnamed Korean rumor; Gagadget reproduces a 24 September post by Tarun Vats crediting Lanzuk.
claims.assessment: If the entry configuration really moves to 12 GB and 256 GB, the base model loses its 8 GB tier for good, and that is the consequential part of this. The accounts are not independent: three trace to the same Korean supply-chain talk and one is a relay of a relay. No filing, listing or Samsung statement corroborates any of it, and the Pro topping out at 1 TB with 12 GB while the Ultra's 1 TB tier gets 16 GB is odd enough to watch.

claims.title: The family's internal codename moved from Miracle to Trinity
claims.summary: Sammy Fans reports, on SammyGuru's reading of trade data, that the four Galaxy S27 models are now tracked as Trinity1 to Trinity4, replacing the NM1 to NM4 labels that carried the New/Next Miracle codename used for this family earlier in 2026. The mapping is said to be unchanged: base, Plus, Pro and Ultra.
claims.assessment: A codename change mainly shows a programme still being relabelled late in development; it says nothing about shipping hardware. It rests on indirect trade-data reading rather than a document, and it does at least carry the four-model structure forward under new names.

claims.title: Privacy Display may gain a per-app split-screen mode
claims.summary: Ice Universe posted on 24 September that the Galaxy S27 Ultra will adopt the split-screen privacy behaviour Xiaomi shipped on the 18 Pro in China a day earlier: one app in a two-app split view stays protected while the other remains visible, and the protected region follows the window as the divider moves. Android Authority, Sammy Fans and SammyGuru relayed it the same day and Gadget Hacks a day later, all tracing the claim to that single post, in which the leaker also argues Samsung's current S26 Ultra still blocks light more strongly than Xiaomi's implementation.
claims.assessment: This is a software behaviour rather than a panel specification, and every readable account of it goes back to one post. Xiaomi shipping an equivalent makes the behaviour real on another phone, not on Samsung's. It sits apart from this archive's older Privacy Display thread, which is about which models get the hardware at all.

claims.title: The variable-aperture comeback is reported dropped on cost
claims.summary: Tech Advisor's round-up, updated on 25 September, says the variable aperture that early S27 reporting expected has been abandoned under component-cost pressure, and that the Ultra gives up its 10-megapixel 3x telephoto rather than gaining a lens. The page lists ETNews, Digital Chat Station, Smart Pikachu, Ice Universe, GalaxyClub, Phonefuturist and Roland Quandt as its sources, and separately gives Pro dimensions of 154.06 x 73.77 x 7.95 mm against the Ultra's 163.76 x 78.25 x 7.97 mm, figures that trace to the OnLeaks CAD set this archive already holds.
claims.assessment: Cost-cutting is the most repeated explanation in this record for the camera changes, which makes the reading plausible rather than proven. The page also contradicts itself: its summary bullets still advertise a variable-aperture comeback while its body reports the idea dropped, so only the dropped reading is recorded. The archive never published a settled variable-aperture claim, so nothing existing is being reversed.

claims.title: The Exynos 2700 enters wafer production on a 10% larger order
claims.summary: The Elec reports Samsung began full-scale front-end wafer production of the Exynos 2700 in early October, at a volume more than 10% above the Exynos 2600's, because a fourth S27 model now needs the chip. GSMArena, SamMobile, Android Headlines and Sammy Fans relay it the same day: the base S27, S27 Plus and the new S27 Pro get Exynos in Korea and Europe, the United States and China stay on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, and no decision has been taken on the Ultra. The reported three-to-four-month wafer-to-product interval is read as consistent with a February or March 2027 launch.
claims.assessment: One Korean industry-sourcing chain, published by a semiconductor trade outlet rather than a phone blog, and internally consistent across the relays — but every relay traces to The Elec and none inspected an order book or a part. Wafer starts date a programme; they do not settle the chip names, the regional mix or the Ultra.

claims.title: An Exynos-powered Ultra prototype is reported in testing
claims.summary: SammyGuru reported on 1 October that tipster @kro_roe says a Galaxy S27 Ultra prototype is being tested with an Exynos chip, most likely the Exynos 2700, and that Snapdragon negotiations may have fallen through. Android Headlines wrote the same story a day later, tying it to Samsung's absence from Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit messaging. Both stress that Samsung has not decided which chip the Ultra ships. That reading was reversed on 9 October, when reporting attributed to Lanzuk said the Ultra would stay on Snapdragon worldwide.
claims.assessment: The prototype claim rests on a single tipster account and no outlet has seen the prototype or a chip order for the Ultra, so two write-ups are one chain rather than corroboration. The dispute is genuine inside Samsung: System LSI is pushing the chip and MX is weighing thermals, benchmarks and Qualcomm's price, which would make the Ultra dual-chip for the first time since the S22 Ultra. The prototype report is kept alive: the October production order and the allocation report describe different things, and only the model assignment is disputed.

claims.title: The Ultra's 3x telephoto is reported gone, leaving one 5x module
claims.summary: Ice Universe posted on 29 September that the Galaxy S27 Ultra drops its dedicated 10-megapixel 3x telephoto and keeps only the 50-megapixel 5x periscope, unchanged at a 1/2.52-inch sensor and f/2.9, so the phone jumps from 1x straight to 5x. 9to5Google, Android Authority, SammyGuru and Gagadget relayed it the same day; Gagadget records that the earlier larger 4x sensor rumor now appears dead. OnLeaks' 28 September render shows three rear cameras, which fits the removal.
claims.assessment: Every account of the removal traces to one Ice Universe post, but the three-camera geometry is separately readable in the OnLeaks CAD render, so the count is better supported than the reasoning. That mid-range shots would fall back on cropping the main sensor is the outlets' inference, not something the leak states, and Samsung has said nothing.

claims.title: A 200-megapixel ISOCELL HP6 is tipped for the Ultra's main camera
claims.summary: Ice Universe says the Ultra's 200-megapixel main camera moves to an ISOCELL HP6, described as a Galaxy-specific version of Samsung's ISOCELL HPC with its DeepPix pixel architecture. The same account reports warmer colour than the S26 Ultra, better retention of small bright highlights on both the main and 5x cameras, and less noise in shadows. Android Authority, SammyGuru and Gagadget relay the claims and note they come from one insider.
claims.assessment: A named part with a described architecture is more inspectable than a colour-tuning claim, but there is no part number, datasheet or sample image behind it. The processing half overlaps the archive's earlier @WalleGalaxy thread, which Android Authority itself flagged as not established, so two accounts pointing the same way does not upgrade either.

claims.title: Tipsters disagree where inside the camera pill the telephoto sits
claims.summary: OnLeaks published an updated S27 Ultra rear render on 28 September placing a telephoto lens at the top of the pill, then a microphone, auxiliary sensors and the flash at the bottom. Ice Universe replied that an authoritative source puts the camera at the bottom with the flash above it, and Android Headlines reports Anthony (@TheGalox_) and kro taking the bottom position as well, with kro adding that the telephoto module was redesigned to be smaller.
claims.assessment: This is an argument about the inside of a cutout, which CAD renders show only as openings, so neither reading can be checked from the artwork. The archive holds both and treats the matter as unresolvable before launch; it does not disturb the camera count, which the renders agree on.

claims.title: The Ultra is tipped at 218 grams without getting thicker
claims.summary: Ice Universe says the Galaxy S27 Ultra weighs 218 g and measures 7.9 mm, four grams more than the 214 g S26 Ultra at the same thickness; the August CAD set had given 7.97 mm. GSMArena, Android Authority and Tom's Guide relay the figures and connect the added mass to the reported 5,700 mAh cell.
claims.assessment: One tipster's numbers, though they sit alongside two different shapes of earlier evidence — the CAD dimensions and the reported battery increase. Four grams in an unchanged body is small enough that only a hands-on measurement will settle it, and nothing here confirms weight or thickness.

claims.title: Every S27 model is tipped for a Korean price rise
claims.summary: A Korean post attributed to the Naver leaker Lanzuk, also reported as yeux1122, says the Galaxy S27 line rises across models and storage tiers, with the base increase in the high KRW 130,000 range (about $95) and steeper steps between capacities. GSMArena, 9to5Google, Android Authority and Tom's Guide relay it; GSMArena extrapolates a $1,399 starting Ultra, $1,549 for 512 GB and a 1 TB tier approaching $2,000, while Android Authority gives a KRW 100,000 to 130,000 range (about $74 to $96). The earlier expectation that only the Ultra would move is contradicted.
claims.assessment: Price is the easiest claim to guess and the hardest to confirm before listings; the figures are Korean-market only, and the outlets themselves flag the clash with the earlier Ultra-only reading. Memory costs are the stated cause on every account, and 9to5Google notes the post does not say whether the increase is linear or compounds across storage tiers.

claims.title: Screen-protector listings put the four fronts close to the S26
claims.summary: Third-party screen protectors for the family surfaced in late September and early October. SammyGuru read retail listings showing the base S27 and the S27 Pro nearly the same height with the Pro slightly wider, the S27 Plus larger again and the Ultra the biggest. Sammy Fans relayed both that reading and an Ice Universe image of five S27 Ultra protectors that may be interchangeable with the S26 Ultra's. The sizes line up with the earlier ETNews panel figures of 6.27, 6.47, 6.66 and 6.89 inches.
claims.assessment: Accessory listings are a real artifact but a weak one: they are made from the same leak ecosystem, can simply be wrong, and the outlets themselves caution that protectors are not design drawings. The useful signal is that the front is expected to change little, which fits the archive's render-based reading rather than adding independent evidence to it.

claims.title: Component and panel production for the family is reported underway
claims.summary: Sammy Fans relays a ZDNet report that some Galaxy S27 components went into production in September with a broader build-out in October, that Samsung Display is starting OLED panel output this month against a target of roughly 47–48 million panels (more than 10% above the S26 target, with 2–3 million Pro panels by the end of 2026), and that some Galaxy S26 parts will be reused as memory prices climb.
claims.assessment: A supply-chain report rather than a product claim, and the panel figures are a target rather than an outcome. It matters because it dates the programme: a parts ramp now is consistent with the February–March 2027 window the archive already holds, and it is the first evidence here that the fourth model is being built rather than merely rumoured.

claims.title: The Ultra's colours drop purple for light pink, with a special Violet added
claims.summary: Ice Universe posted on 5 October that the Galaxy S27 Ultra's base colours are Black, Blue, Light Pink and White, then added a special Violet later the same day. Android Authority, 9to5Google, SamMobile and Sammy Fans all relayed the post within a day and each expects further online-store exclusive shades on top. Light Pink would replace the Cobalt Violet that headlined the S26 Ultra and leave the Ultra without a purple-family finish for the first time since the S23 Ultra's Lavender; 9to5Google reads the list as purple leaving the lineup while Android Authority's update treats the Violet as a special edition rather than a base colour, so both readings are kept.
claims.assessment: One tipster post with no document, filing or render behind it, and every readable account here is a relay of that same post, so the agreement adds reach rather than confirmation. Exact shades, how many online-exclusive options follow and which markets get them are all unstated.

claims.title: The Ultra keeps 60 W but is tipped to hold high power for longer
claims.summary: WalleGalaxy claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra keeps the S26 Ultra's 60 W wired ceiling while sustaining roughly 55 W to 56 W for longer during the early part of the cycle, which Android Authority reads as about 2% to 3% faster charging despite the larger 5,700 mAh cell. Geeky Gadgets repeated the figures on 9 October, and Tech Advisor's 8 October update carries the same numbers in a round-up whose source list credits phonefuturist and Ice Universe instead. Nothing is cited beyond the accounts themselves, and the claim is narrower than a wattage increase: the ceiling stays where the 3C certification put it.
claims.assessment: Restated by several outlets but traceable to a single leaker post, and the outlets do not even agree on which account made it. The certified 60 W ceiling, the rumoured sustained curve and the resulting charge-time estimate are kept as separate facts, and no real-world charging test exists yet.

claims.title: The Ultra is now reported to stay Snapdragon-only worldwide
claims.summary: On 9 October, coverage attributed to the Naver blogger Lanzuk said Samsung has no plans to put the Exynos 2700 in the Galaxy S27 Ultra in any market, keeping the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 for Galaxy across regions, with the Exynos 2700 going to the S27, S27+ and S27 Pro in most of Europe, Asia and Africa and Snapdragon reserved mainly for North America and China. SammyGuru, Sammy Fans, Nokia Power User and Samsung Magazine relayed it the same day, and Android Headlines published the same reading under a title that treats the question as closed. It sits directly against the 1 and 2 October accounts of an Exynos-powered Ultra prototype in testing and of an Exynos production order already tied to the Ultra question. On 17 October Sammy Fans reported that Samsung has not yet decided the Ultra's chip and that Snapdragon could still remain, which weakens the 'no plans' framing without supplying a document in either direction.
claims.assessment: Both directions rest on unattributed Korean supply-chain talk read through relays, and Samsung has said nothing. This report does not dispute the Exynos 2700 production order or its higher volume, only which models receive the chip, so the archive keeps the prototype and production claims alive and records this as contradicting them rather than superseding them.

claims.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is reported to overheat in Ultra testing
claims.summary: Seoul Economic Daily reported on 16 October that Samsung's MX division found Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 exceeding thermal thresholds and throttling under sustained load in Galaxy S27 Ultra verification, asked Qualcomm for a fix by mid-October, and could fall back to the Exynos 2700 if one does not arrive. 9to5Google, Android Authority and SamMobile relayed the report the same day. Qualcomm called the account inaccurate, with CMO Don McGuire saying there are no systemic thermal issues; Gizmochina noted that his public reply named the standard 8 Elite Gen 6 rather than the Extreme variant at issue.
claims.assessment: The core report comes from a named Korean business outlet citing multiple industry sources, is specific about the deadline and the fallback, and is not an anonymous aggregator. It is still unattributed supply-chain testimony that this archive cannot inspect, and the company that would know denies it. The denial does not show the tests passed, and the report does not establish that any retail device overheats. Neither the throttle figures nor the Exynos fallback is treated as settled.

claims.title: Bezel and camera-bump measurements arrive with a disputed baseline
claims.summary: Ice Universe posted measurements on 15 October putting the Galaxy S27 Ultra's display bezel at 1.28 mm and its rear camera bump at 4.69 mm. GSMArena, Gizmochina, SamMobile and Notebookcheck relayed them but disagreed about the comparison: GSMArena gave the S26 Ultra 1.15 mm bezels, while SamMobile and Gizmochina gave 1.32 mm, so the same S27 figure was read as thicker in one place and slimmer in another. Sammy Fans separately attributed 1.21 mm bezels and a 4.64 mm bump to @OnLeaks, alongside a 7.97 mm body and 12.61 mm total, which matches neither Ice Universe figure.
claims.assessment: Two well-known accounts are being quoted with overlapping but different numbers, and at least one outlet has merged them. The direction of the camera-bump change is consistent across the reports; the bezel direction depends on which S26 Ultra baseline is correct, and the archive cannot settle that from these pages. Fractions of a millimetre are below what a render or a case can verify.

claims.title: UWB is listed for the Pro and Ultra, and missing from the base and Plus
claims.summary: Abhishek Yadav (@yabhishekhd) reported Chinese MIIT certification entries for all four S27 models in which only the S27 Pro and S27 Ultra list ultra-wideband support. Android Authority, SamMobile and GSMArena relayed the reading on 16 October. The base model has never carried UWB; the Plus has had it since the S21+, so its omission would be the notable change. SamMobile notes that the documents may be preliminary or may simply omit the feature, and that Bluetooth 6.0 channel sounding could offer a less precise alternative.
claims.assessment: A regulatory listing is firmer than a render, but this archive did not read the MIIT entries, the model-number mapping comes from one tipster, and absence from a filing is weaker evidence than a positive listing. The claim is recorded as a reported downgrade, not an established one, and Samsung has said nothing.

claims.title: The 16MP selfie upgrade is now tipped for the Pro and Ultra only
claims.summary: GalaxyClub reported in mid-October that the Galaxy S27 and S27+ will keep the 12MP autofocus front camera used since the S23 series, while the S27 Pro and S27 Ultra get a new 16MP sensor that may be square. SamMobile, Android Authority, PhoneArena and Sammy Fans relayed it on 14 and 15 October. The report cites no source, and the square format remains unconfirmed even for the two higher models.
claims.assessment: This narrows the archive's July 16MP selfie report rather than contradicting it: that claim concerned the Ultra, and GalaxyClub's earlier account left the base and Plus open. The tiering is specific and consistent across relays but rests on one publication's unsourced report, so the base and Plus figures are treated as likely but unverified, and the sensor shape as unresolved.

claims.title: DC dimming is tipped for the Pro and Ultra
claims.summary: Tipster @WalleGalaxy reported that the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra will support DC dimming, which adjusts current instead of pulsing the panel and can reduce the flicker some users see at low brightness. GSMArena, SammyGuru and PhoneArena relayed it between 10 and 12 October. The reports expect a hybrid implementation, with DC at higher brightness and PWM retained at low brightness, because low-voltage OLED output distorts colour; GSMArena notes the Galaxy S24 FE used a similar split.
claims.assessment: A specific, technically plausible claim from one tipster, with outlets adding context rather than independent evidence. No panel specification, supplier document or Samsung statement supports it, and the brightness range where DC applies is unknown. The archive treats it as a reported feature, not a confirmed one.

claims.title: A second-generation Privacy Display is tipped to fix clarity and angles
claims.summary: SammyGuru reported on 12 October, citing tipster @Sawyergalox, that Samsung is developing a second-generation Privacy Display for the S27 Ultra and possibly the Pro, improving viewing angles, resolution and clarity while the privacy filter is active. PhoneArena's 10 October piece describes the same complaints about the S26 Ultra's implementation — washed-out colour and a resolution hit — and says Samsung is working on them, without naming the tipster.
claims.assessment: Both pages describe an improvement to a feature the archive already records as expected on the Pro and Ultra, but the specific second-generation claims trace to one tipster account with no document. The existence of the complaint is better supported than the fix, and no target specification is given.

claims.title: A second October ladder puts the base S27 at $1,099 and the Ultra at $1,499
claims.summary: On 13 October SammyGuru and Sammy Fans reported a price roadmap attributed to Anthony (@TheGalox_) giving $1,099 for the Galaxy S27, $1,199 for the S27+, $1,399 for the S27 Pro and $1,499 for the S27 Ultra, with memory costs as the stated cause. That is $200 above the S26 launch prices for the base and Ultra in the comparison both outlets use, and it contradicts the 8 October @phonefuturist ladder of $899, $1,099, $1,299 and $1,399. Sammy Fans' prose once gives the Pro as $1,199 while its own list and SammyGuru both say $1,399.
claims.assessment: Two tipster ladders five days apart cannot both be right, and neither is a listing or filing. The newer one is internally inconsistent in one relay, which lowers confidence further. The archive keeps both and notes that the shared direction — higher prices driven by memory supply — is the only part the two accounts agree on.

sources.provenance: Attributes the increases to the Korean blogger yeux1122 and gives a KRW 100,000 to 130,000 range (about $74 to $96) applying to Korea only; repeats the leaker's earlier LPDDR6 and UFS 5.1 claim as context.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra's missing camera shown in leaks is its 3x zoom
sources.provenance: Reproduces Ice Universe's 29 September X post and OnLeaks' 28 September render thread and compares the new camera island with the S26 Ultra's four rear sensors; neither original post was read.

sources.title: Latest Galaxy S27 Ultra leak brings good news for low-light shots, bad news for zoom
sources.provenance: Relays Ice Universe's claims on the ISOCELL HP6 main sensor, warmer colour, improved highlight handling on the main and 5x cameras, lower shadow noise and the removal of the 3x telephoto.

sources.title: Massive Galaxy S27 Ultra Camera Leak Reveals Key Upgrades (3x Zoom is Gone)
sources.provenance: The fullest write-up of the same Ice Universe material; treats the three-camera renders as confirming the 3x removal and adds that the 5x sensor and f/2.9 aperture are carried over from the S26 Ultra.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra leak: no 3x zoom camera, warmer photos
sources.provenance: States that the earlier larger 4x sensor rumor now appears dead and that mid-range zoom would rely on cropping, which it labels an inference rather than a leaked fact; also carries a reported $1,300 starting price that this archive does not treat as a listing.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra camera mystery deepens as leakers clash over new render
sources.provenance: Details OnLeaks' 28 September render, Ice Universe's analysis of four Chinese case molds and its reply from an unnamed authoritative source, and explains why CAD renders cannot settle flush component positions.

sources.title: Tipsters Can't Agree on Where the Galaxy S27 Ultra's Telephoto Camera Sits
sources.provenance: Names Anthony (@TheGalox_) and kro as holding the bottom-mounted telephoto reading against OnLeaks, and records kro's claim that the telephoto module was redesigned smaller.

sources.title: Exclusive: Galaxy S27 Series Screen Protectors Reveal Size and Design
sources.provenance: Reads third-party retail screen-protector listings for all four models and reports the base S27 and S27 Pro as near-identical in height with the Pro slightly wider; the sizes are matched to earlier panel figures rather than measured.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra screen protector offers a peek at S26 Ultra design similarity
sources.provenance: Relays an Ice Universe image of five third-party S27 Ultra protectors and suggests they may be interchangeable with the S26 Ultra's; the article itself cautions the accessories are not exact design or dimension matches.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 series screen protector leak shows size differences
sources.provenance: Repeat of the SammyGuru screen-protector reading with images credited to SammyGuru and the four display sizes repeated from earlier reporting.

sources.title: Samsung starts Galaxy S27 component production: Report
sources.provenance: Relays a ZDNet report dated 2 October: some components went into production in September with an October ramp, Samsung Display is starting OLED output against roughly 47–48 million panels, and some Galaxy S26 parts will be reused as memory prices rise.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra colors leak, and Samsung could be breaking up with purple (Update: Special color)
sources.provenance: Relays a 5 October post by Ice Universe on X and was updated the same morning to add a special Violet alongside the four base colours. No shade reference, document or filing is cited.

sources.title: Leaked Galaxy S27 Ultra color list doesn't include Purple, for a change
sources.provenance: Reads the same Ice Universe post, compares the list with the purple-family finishes every Ultra has carried since the S23 Ultra, and expects online-exclusive colours to be added on top.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra coming in these five incredible colors
sources.provenance: Same-day write-up of the Ice Universe post; adds that the special Violet may be an online-store exclusive and that its market availability is unknown.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra color options leak
sources.provenance: Relays the same tipster post and lists the S26 Ultra's four standard colours plus two online exclusives for comparison. The page carries a site-wide last-updated banner reading 5 October 2026 12:51 UTC+02:00 rather than an article date; the banner and the body agree here.

sources.title: Samsung may have found a smart way to speed up Galaxy S27 Ultra charging
sources.provenance: Attributes the charging-curve claim to leaker WalleGalaxy and frames it against the iPhone 18 Pro Max's figures; the original post was not read and no certification or document is cited.

sources.title: Samsung's Galaxy S27 Ultra Leak Details Fresh Colors and Faster Charging Speeds
sources.provenance: Second-hand round-up crediting an account it calls Demon's Tech; repeats the 55-56 W sustained figure, the 2-3% charge-time gain and the four-colour palette without pointing at an original post or filing.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 latest rumours: The price could be eye-watering
sources.provenance: Continuously updated round-up read on 8 October. It carries the same 55-56 W sustained-charging figures under a source list naming phonefuturist and Ice Universe rather than WalleGalaxy, and repeats the M16 and M14 display split, the 5,700 mAh Ultra cell, the 5,200 mAh Pro cell, the dropped variable aperture and the four-colour palette.

sources.title: There's a clear divide between Galaxy S27 tiers, as the latest leak lists price
sources.provenance: Reads a @phonefuturist post through Android Headlines: a US ladder of $899, $1,099, $1,299 and $1,399, and an OLED split giving the base and Plus an M14+ panel and the Pro and Ultra the M16 panel. The underlying Android Headlines page could not be opened in this run.

sources.title: New rumors shed light on display tech and price of Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro, and S27 Ultra
sources.provenance: Reads the same @phonefuturist post as carrying global and Korean columns of $999, $1,199, $1,399 and $1,499 to $1,549, and repeats the post's own caveat that the figures are not final while memory and component supply are unsettled.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 pricing leak reveals how all the new models will sit
sources.provenance: Third readable relay of the same X post; notes that the new Pro would launch where the S26 Ultra launched, that the Ultra could then cost $100 more, and that the US base price implies Samsung may avoid another across-the-board increase.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra May Not Get Exynos 2700 After All
sources.provenance: Attributes the reversal to what it calls a renowned Korean leaker without naming a handle in the text, ties the higher Exynos 2700 production volume to the S27 Pro rather than the Ultra, and speculates about capacity and trust as reasons. The underlying post was not read.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra dropping Exynos 2700 for Snapdragon chip in all countries?
sources.provenance: Names Naver blogger Lanzuk as the source of the claim that Samsung has no plans to put the Exynos 2700 in the Ultra, and sets out the regional split for the other three models. The original Naver post was not read.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra Reportedly Ditching Exynos 2700 for Worldwide Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Rollout
sources.provenance: Names Lanzuk on Naver and gives the allocation as Exynos 2700 for the base, Plus and Pro across Europe, Asia and Africa with Snapdragon mainly for North America and China. It reproduces a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 specification table but cites no document; the post itself was not read.

sources.title: Another change of plan? Galaxy S27 Ultra will eventually be available worldwide with a Snapdragon chip
sources.provenance: European relay that credits Lanzuk on Naver and reads the change as Samsung reverting to its usual regional strategy; it adds no document, filing or original post.

sources.title: Overheating in Qualcomm's Next Chip Clouds Galaxy S27 Ultra Plans
sources.provenance: Original Korean business-daily report, read in its English edition, citing multiple unnamed industry sources: Samsung's MX division found the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 exceeding thermal thresholds and throttling in S27 Ultra verification, asked Qualcomm for a fix by mid-October, and may use the Exynos 2700 if it is not resolved. The page was updated on 17 October and carries Qualcomm's denial. It names no document, test log or person.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 reportedly skips Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 due to overheating
sources.provenance: Relays the Seoul Economic Daily report and quotes Qualcomm's statement sent to the outlet. It also notes the Motorola Signature 27 is already shipping on the chip, which the report does not address.

sources.title: Blame Snapdragon: An Exynos-powered Galaxy S27 Ultra is now more likely than ever (Update: Qualcomm statement)
sources.provenance: Reads the Seoul Economic Daily report, adds that Samsung planned to finalise component design by mid-October for a year-end production start, and was updated the same day with Qualcomm's statement. It states that whether Samsung drops Snapdragon entirely or keeps it in some regions is unknown.

sources.title: [Updated] Snapdragon heating issues could force Samsung to use Exynos in Galaxy S27 Ultra
sources.provenance: Relays the same report, adds that the Exynos 2700 is a 10-core part on Samsung Foundry's SF2P node, and carries Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire's denial that the reports are accurate. No test data is reproduced.

sources.title: Qualcomm denies Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 overheating allegations on Galaxy S27 Ultra, but there's a catch
sources.provenance: Quotes McGuire's follow-up on X, which refers to the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 rather than the Extreme variant named in the overheating reports, and records separate reports of crashes and reboots on other phones using the chip. It offers no test evidence either way.

sources.title: Tipster says Galaxy S27 Ultra will have slightly thicker bezels than S26 Ultra
sources.provenance: Relays Ice Universe's measurements: 1.28 mm bezels against 1.15 mm on the S26 Ultra, and a 4.69 mm camera bump against 4.5 mm. It repeats the 163.76 x 78.25 x 7.97 mm dimensions and 218 g weight from earlier reporting. The original post was not read.

sources.title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra will have slimmer display bezels but a thicker camera housing
sources.provenance: Reads the same Ice Universe data but gives the S26 Ultra's bezels as 1.32 mm, so the same 1.28 mm figure becomes a reduction, and gives the S26 Ultra camera housing as roughly 4.5 to 4.6 mm. The body text twice repeats a paragraph about the front, and misnames the coming family as the S26 line in one sentence.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra: Thicker camera bump and slightly thinner display bezels, according to leak
sources.provenance: Reads Ice Universe as giving 1.28 mm bezels, 0.04 mm less than the S26 Ultra, and a 4.69 mm bump against the roughly 4.56 mm in OnLeaks' CAD set. It compares the bezel figure with the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and Oppo Find X10 Pro Max. The original post was not read.

sources.title: Insider leaks Galaxy S27 Ultra design details including camera bump, thickness and bezels
sources.provenance: Attributes a different set of numbers to @OnLeaks: 7.97 mm without the bump, 12.61 mm with it, a 4.64 mm bump and 1.21 mm bezels. It does not reconcile them with the Ice Universe figures published the same day.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra tipped to have slimmer bezel while camera bump increases a bit
sources.provenance: Relays the 1.28 mm and 4.69 mm figures, gives the S26 Ultra 1.32 mm bezels, and sets the 4.69 mm bump against the 4.56 mm in earlier OnLeaks CAD work. It names Ice Universe as the source and links two posts, neither of which was read.

sources.title: The Galaxy S27 Plus could break nearly six years of tradition with this downgrade
sources.provenance: Attributes the MIIT reading to Abhishek Yadav on X: UWB listed for the Pro and Ultra, absent from the base and Plus. It explains what UWB enables for SmartTag 3, Pixel Tag and car or home keys, and notes the filings do not establish global specifications.

sources.title: Galaxy S27+ could lose a feature Samsung has offered for years
sources.provenance: Same MIIT reading via Abhishek Yadav, with the caveat that the documents may be preliminary and may simply omit UWB, and that Bluetooth 6.0 channel sounding could be an alternative. It notes the base model has never had UWB while the Plus has since the S21+.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27+ might miss out on UWB
sources.provenance: Relays the four-model MIIT listing and the Pro-and-Ultra-only UWB reading, and raises the possibility of a mistake in the listing. It gives no model numbers.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus may miss out on selfie camera upgrade
sources.provenance: Relays the tiering without naming GalaxyClub or any other source: 12MP for the S27 and S27+, a possible new 16MP front camera for the Pro and Ultra, possibly square. It also repeats the three-camera rear setup with a 200MP main, 50MP ultrawide and 50MP periscope.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 and S27+ to miss out on Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra front camera upgrade
sources.provenance: Names GalaxyClub as the source and states that GalaxyClub cites none. It sets out the expected rear-camera split and says the 16MP sensor's size and format are unclear.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus will reportedly miss out on a key camera upgrade
sources.provenance: Also reads GalaxyClub, notes that the publication previously reported the 16MP sensor for the higher models without deciding on the base and Plus, and points out that GalaxyClub cites no source for the new tiering.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus rumored to miss on an exciting camera upgrade
sources.provenance: Reads the translated Galaxy Club report, repeats that no source is cited, and compares the tiering with Pixel and iPhone selfie hardware. It says the 12MP sensor has been used since the S23 series.

sources.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 might finally introduce DC dimming
sources.provenance: Reports that the S27 Pro and Ultra will offer DC dimming, likely in a hybrid scheme with PWM at low brightness, and ties it to the M16 panel tier and the retention of Privacy Display on the same two models. It does not name the tipster in the body and did not read the original post.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra May Fix OLED Flickering and Privacy Display Issues
sources.provenance: Attributes DC dimming to @WalleGalaxy and the second-generation Privacy Display to @Sawyergalox, saying the latter could improve viewing angles, resolution and clarity. It adds that Samsung is consulting display-safety companies and that a true 10-bit panel is only chatter. Neither post was read.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra is getting three awesome display upgrades that have me excited
sources.provenance: Opinion-led write-up of the DC dimming report, adding that the S24 FE used a PWM and DC split, that Samsung's flagship PWM tops out around 480 Hz, and that the M16 panel also goes to the iPhone 18 Pro. It says Samsung is working on Privacy Display complaints without naming a source for that part.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Price Leak Points to a Major Hike Across the Lineup
sources.provenance: Repeats an X rumor without naming the account in the body: $1,099, $1,199, $1,399 and $1,499 for the four models, framed against S26 prices and the memory supply crunch. It calls the figures estimates and gives no market or storage tier.

sources.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra rumored to cost hefty $1,499; S27 price to hit $1,099
sources.provenance: Names Anthony (@TheGalox_) as the source, gives the same four figures, and says the base and Ultra rise $200 while the Plus rises $100. Its prose once gives the Pro as $1,199, contradicting its own list and the other relay. No market, storage tier or document is specified.

sources.title: Another Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra case leak reveals upgraded camera design
sources.provenance: Describes a video posted by @UniverseIce showing another S27 Ultra case with a horizontal camera bar, and says the layout resembles earlier leaks. It repeats the three-camera and 200MP main claims without new detail and does not link the post directly.

sources.title: New report suggests Snapdragon chip's exclusivity on Galaxy S27 Ultra next year
sources.provenance: Says Samsung has not decided the Ultra's processor, that its chip division wants Exynos while its phone division is checking heat, capacity and cost, and that Snapdragon could therefore stay. It repeats the 10%-higher Exynos 2700 production and an internal Geekbench 6 multi-core advantage of about 9.5%, without naming the underlying report.
